ProSights created a shared work-order ID across RailcarRX, ADP and Sage, tagged every service order with location, car type, car age, customer, supplier and parts, and built an operating scorecard that management and the sponsor read from the same numbers.

The ERP held about 25 broad service types and nothing about the car, the parts, the labor or the shop. Reporting ran through 35 Excel workbooks linked by lookup formulas and refreshed a few times a year for board meetings. On that view paint and blast and rubber linings looked unprofitable, and management planned to cut both.

We started with one question the CFO already had, why gross margin had fallen against the prior year. We linked each service order across the three systems, grouped similar jobs by service, shop, car type, age and supplier, and compared each group with the prior year and the weighted average, so finance could see the decline at job level before anyone cut a service.

A matching layer that creates and maintains the shared order ID. A tagged record for every service order, from request form through parts and labor to the paid invoice. An operating scorecard with four KPI groups, demand, throughput, cycle time and unit economics, baselined on prior year and refreshed from the source systems. A selected view of the same data for the sponsor.
Sources: RailcarRX, ADP, Sage. Process: Shared work-order ID, Validate matches, Human review. Destinations: Job-level scorecard.
A two-week diagnostic, findings in writing, a plan priced by milestone.
AP and bank reconciliation across 35 subsidiaries | ProSights

A railcar services roll-up ran finance 35 times over. About 550 supplier invoices a month were typed and coded by hand across company folders, with vendors set up differently in each subsidiary. Around 90 bank accounts were reconciled one at a time against Sage, and unexplained differences carried into the next month. Nobody checked an invoice price against the purchase order it paid.
ProSights built one invoice workflow and one reconciliation queue across all subsidiaries, with every extracted value linked to its source page and staff reviewing only the items that fail a check.

We took the two recurring processes with the clearest baseline, measured them per invoice and per account, and agreed the matching and coding rules with the controller before automating anything. Review stayed with the finance team. The workflows prepare records and route exceptions, and staff approve before anything posts to Sage.
Sources: Supplier invoices, Purchase orders, Bank statements, Sage. Process: Invoice checks, Reconciliation, Finance approval. Destinations: Approved Sage export, Exception queue.
A two-week diagnostic, findings in writing, a plan priced by milestone.

ProSights matches SOWs, purchase orders and order forms to customer accounts and project records, extracts commercial terms with citations to the source page, and compares planned scope and hours against actuals from the services system in one review workspace.

Customer names and IDs differed between the documents, Salesforce and the services system, so a purchase order could not be attached with confidence to the project it paid for. Some documents carried a Salesforce ID, others only a customer name, a signing ID or a date, and the matching rules had never been written down. Historical order forms and SOWs had never been structured.
Sources: PDFs — SOWs and POs, Salesforce — Customer accounts, Services system — Project hours.

ProSights extracted every contract term with a citation to the clause it came from, validated it against a defined schema, loaded it into Salesforce without overwriting existing records, and reconciled the result to ARR for board reporting.

Multi-year agreements had been split into annual records. No identifier tied a CRM record to the signed agreement that governed it, so every correction was manual. The previous vendor had delivered the migration and left, and finance could not reconcile ARR from the CRM to the balance sheet.

A reasoning-based extraction engine that reads footnotes, tables and handwriting in four languages. A human review surface with the source clause beside every value. A re-runnable pipeline that can be pointed at the next acquisition. A reconciliation of contract ARR to the balance sheet.
Sources: Signed agreements — 5 formats, 4 languages. Process: Extract with citations, Validate, Human review. Destinations: Salesforce agreements, ARR reconciliation.
A two-week diagnostic, findings in writing, a plan priced by milestone.
